newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Tanzania air to be privatised by end '98-ATC chief.
newsitem.headline: Tanzania air to be privatised by end '98-ATC chief.

text.p: State-owned Air Tanzania Corporation aims to be privatised before the end of 1998, its chief executive said on Sunday.
"We hope we'll be able to privatise this corporation before the end of next year," ATC chairman Abbas Sykes told Reuters.

Sykes said a coalition of Malaysian investors had expressed an interest in acquiring a share of the airline once it is offered for sale. He would also seek talks with Germany's Lufthansa for a possible joint venture.
Sykes said Tanzania was interested in concluding a deal similar to that in which the Dutch airline KLM took a 26 percent stake in Kenya Airways.
Sykes said moves to attract British Airways as a partner were unsuccessful. "They are not interested. They don't need us because they are quite comfortable where they are," he said.

The ATC chairman said he would not seek a merger with Alliance Airlines, in which the Tanzanian and Ugandan government each hold a 30 percent stake with the remaining equity held by South African Airways.
Sykes said he feared a deal with Alliance would pave the way for South African domination of sub-Saharan skies.
He said ATC, owners of two Boeing 737-200s and two Fokker F-27 turbo-props, had shown a modest profit since economic reforms were implemented in 1992.
